result:
I accept the package, with two wording conditions and one correction to my first answer. I have now read the technique-selection source, `templates/profile.md` and `templates/toolbox.md`. I did not open `external-ecc/`, so my ECC position relies on your summary of those files.

| # | Your point | My position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Dependencies | **Accept.** My blanket default was stronger than POLICY §5 supports. Use your wording: follow the project's dependency policy and the task's authority, and escalate additions that are consequential or unapproved. |
| 2 | Prose sections, not frontmatter | **Accept.** Add optional "Exclusions / behaviour to preserve" and "References / starting read paths" under the existing task sections. `scope` and the checkpoint's Evidence line stay authoritative. Review covers exclusions through the existing scope check. |
| 3 | Bug recipe | **Accept.** It matches the source's "where practical" wording at line 48. It adds no lighter authority gate. |
| 4 | Techniques | **Accept**, with a correction to my first answer. The source makes refactoring part of TDD (line 90), so I was wrong to call the skill's "refactoring is not part of the loop" rule acceptable. The installed `tdd` skill is a differing variant. Use a short list of optional examples in the Approach guidance. Prefer real red/green/refactor for clear logic, and allow in-scope refactoring while the checks stay green. The "confirm seams with the user" step needs no fresh owner approval. It maps to the task or design record. |
| 5 | Product-AI sentence | **Accept.** I misread §12: recurrence is a factor to weigh, not a threshold. One conditional sentence is proportionate. It belongs in the profile's Quality expectations or Delivery guidance and in the design verification section. It should not go in readiness gate logic. Pilot the datasets, the scoring and the tooling later. |
| 6 | Test accounts | **Accept.** The wording should say dedicated test accounts, never the owner's real accounts. App roles are allowed as the journey requires. The accounts carry no repository, workflow-approval or production-data power. There is no default auth bypass. The harness login limit is tool-specific, and I'm relying on your verification of Claude Chrome's documentation. |
| 7 | Glossary, skills, extra test designer | **Accept.** A glossary is acceptable when an approved record designates or links it as canonical. Defer both skills until a task needs them. Defer the extra test designer for high-consequence work. |
| ECC | Pass on the bundle | **Accept on your evidence.** Your summary lists mandatory TDD, an 80% coverage rule, parallelism rules and an `@latest` MCP executable. These conflict with POLICY's requirement to pin external tools and with the package's rejection of universal TDD and coverage quotas. Reference its contract and browser ideas only. No toolbox entry is needed, because nothing is adopted. |

**Two conditions remain. They are about wording, and I do not oppose any item:**

1. **Test data and evidence.** The UI-verification sentence should require test data only, and it should keep secrets and tokens out of screenshots and traces. It should also restate once that running the app is layer-1 evidence and does not replace review, integration verification or owner acceptance. An admin-role test account must point at a non-production environment, or at a production tenant scoped to test data. Without that, admin testing touches real data.
2. **Credential location.** The profile's Execution section should hold only a reference to secret storage, never a credential value. This matches `procedures/identity.md`.

**One disagreement is left for the owner.** The owner's phrase "credentials … provided by me" has to be narrowed to dedicated test accounts. This is the one place where the package declines something the owner literally asked for. The backlog status should therefore be "Partly adopted" with this caveat called out. It should not be folded into the approval without mention.

The defer and reject lists stand as you stated them. The whole package is still a recommendation. It needs a maintenance record, independent review, owner approval, a new workflow version and explicit project adoption before anything changes.
